title: I built a market scanner that watches volume instead of price — 6 months in, here's what's under the hood
author: AvailableAlarm2171
selftext:
I got tired of finding out about moves after they happened. Top-gainer lists are a record of the past — by the time something is on one, the volume that caused it arrived minutes or hours earlier.

So I built a scanner that watches the volume instead. It's been running about six months. This is a technical write-up, not a pitch; I'll be upfront that it's a paid product at the bottom and you can ignore that part entirely.

What it does

It tracks roughly a thousand exchange pairs and nine thousand on-chain pools, and looks for a specific thing: a minute where volume hits three times its own recent average on at least $500 of real turnover. That's the entire trigger. No prediction, no proprietary indicator — just noticing quickly when something quiet stops being quiet.

Some implementation details that might be interesting:

* Every coin is compared against itself, not a global average. A global comparison only ever surfaces the same handful of large caps. A small coin doing 4× its own two-week norm is interesting; the same absolute number from BTC is a Tuesday.
* Bursts read the live trade stream, not candles. A one-second burst is visible before it has finished becoming a one-minute candle.
* The DEX side reads swap events directly off Solana, BNB Chain, Base and Arbitrum with my own indexer, rather than re-publishing another aggregator's feed. That was a lot more work and I'd probably do it again.
* One WebSocket carries every price tick to the browser, so the page holds a single connection instead of polling per coin.

Things I'll say against it, since nobody else will

* The retrospective "what the scanner caught" list shows peak and current price side by side, deliberately. It is not a win rate — losing signals aren't in it, and I say that on the page itself. Anyone showing you only the peak is selling you something.
* Volume spikes are noisy. Plenty of them are nothing. It's a filter for attention, not a buy signal, and it will never be one.
* It doesn't do prediction, price targets, or "AI picks that moon". If that's what you're after, this isn't it.

Some things I got badly wrong, since the failures are more useful than the wins:

For three days I stored the wrong volume field from one exchange — the token count instead of the dollar value. A coin priced at three ten-billionths of a dollar showed up as having traded 749 billion in a minute. Real figure: about $254. Every threshold in the product is denominated in that number, so for three days it was enthusiastically pointing at the cheapest garbage on the exchange. Fix: derive the field instead of trusting the docs — base × price == quote settles it in ten seconds.

Separately, two exchange feeds dropped at 02:23 one night and never reconnected, because I'd written the disconnect handler to log a warning and nothing else. 506 coins sat frozen for twelve hours and nothing alerted, because from outside there is no difference between a stale price and a quiet market.

Disclosure: this is my own project and it's paid — there's a $0.99 day pass and longer plans after that. I'm not going to link it in the post body; it's in my profile and I'll answer anything in the comments. Genuinely more interested in talking about the volume-field problem, because I suspect I'm not the only one who's been bitten by exchange field semantics.
